# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Member:** Quinn Iverson
**Member ID:** W154693844
**Payer/Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Denial date:** 2026-08-14
**Reference number:** POC-E14E3A00BC-47205
**Governing policy:** Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which was denied on 2026-08-14 (reference number POC-E14E3A00BC-47205). My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I understand this to mean the plan applied its own criteria for total ankle arthroplasty. Those criteria, from the Small Joint Surgery guideline, state:

> "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present."

I believe my records meet these criteria as follows:

**Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken on 2026-07-17 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.

**Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.** I completed 16 weeks (2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14) of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, totaling 20 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This is longer than the 3-month period referenced in the plan's criteria. In addition, I used NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 that gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief. My function during this time has remained impaired: I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to walking two blocks, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain.

The guideline also states:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document ongoing pain over 18 months and difficulty walking (limited to two blocks), but I do not see a specific numeric VAS pain score in the materials I have reviewed. [Please insert VAS pain score from the clinical record, if documented] should be added to the appeal file if available, since this appears to directly support the functional-impairment element of the plan's own criteria.

**Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.** [Please insert documentation of pedal pulses/vascular perfusion exam findings from the medical record, if available]. I understand this is one of the plan's required elements, and I am asking my surgeon's office to confirm whether this was documented and, if so, to submit it with this appeal.

**Device is FDA approved.** [Please insert confirmation from the surgeon's office that the specific implant/device proposed is FDA approved].

I also note the guideline's general statement that:

> "Carelon applies objective and evidence-based criteria, and takes individual circumstances and the local delivery system into account when determining the medical appropriateness of health care services."

Given the extent of conservative treatment I have already completed — physical therapy, NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection — over an 18-month period, and the radiographic findings of advanced joint damage, I believe my individual circumstances support approval under the plan's own stated criteria.

## What I am asking

I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider and approve prior authorization for the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-10, and I am submitting it within that timeframe. Please send any additional questions or requests for records to me or to my surgeon's office, Dr. Okafor, as needed.

I have submitted this appeal according to the instructions in my denial notice. If the mailing address in this letter is not correct, please direct it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or I can be reached to resubmit as needed.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Iverson**
Member ID: W154693844

---

21 Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:
If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented.

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable.

For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes.
Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended.

Where there are patient-specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient a shared decision-making process with the patient to discuss these modifiable comorbidities is strongly recommended and should be documented.
